title: TheGentlemen ransomware - BYOVD abused driver load (GentleKiller suite)
author: ASSIONGBON Adama SOC & CTI Consultant | https://www.linkedin.com/in/adama-assiongbon-9029893a/
description:
Detects the load of vulnerable / malicious kernel drivers abused by the TheGentlemen ransomware-as-a-service EDR-killer suite (GentleKiller and the integrated HexKiller / ThrottleBlood / HavocKiller). Per ESET research (June 2026), each GentleKiller variant drops and loads a different BYOVD driver to gain kernel privileges and disable security products. This BROAD rule combines driver-filename matching (hunting, false positives possible) with the known sample SHA-1 hashes (high confidence). Use for visibility and to corroborate the STRICT staging rule and the mass-kill correlation.
Telemetry: Sysmon Event ID 6 (Driver loaded). Some driver filenames (e.g. vgk.sys, GameDriverX64.sys, dmx.sys) also belong to legitimate software, so a name-only hit always requires triage; a hash hit is a confirmed TheGentlemen sample.
DETECTION BLIND SPOT: if the actor renames the driver and recompiles (changing the hash), both detection branches are evaded simultaneously. The behavioral correlation rule (process_access) is the only coverage that survives this evasion.
IoC freshness: driver names and hashes may go stale as the actor swaps drivers between campaigns. See ioc/ioc_hashes.csv and ioc/ioc_driver_names.csv for last_verified dates.
